stories.head: Rocket Lab's Iridium deal raises eyebrows
stories.body: Rocket Lab's acquisition of Iridium for an undisclosed amount has been labeled as the 'logical next step' by CEO Peter Beck. This move comes as Rocket Lab aims to bolster its satellite communications capabilities, a sector where competition is heating up. With Iridium's established network, Rocket Lab is positioning itself to capture a larger share of the lucrative communications market.
stories.soWhat: Acquisitions like this often signal that companies are scrambling to consolidate their positions before the next wave of competition emerges.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M amid co-orbital concerns
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding is aimed at enhancing its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, which are increasingly critical as geopolitical tensions escalate. The backing comes primarily from defense-focused investors, underscoring the growing importance of security in space operations.
stories.soWhat: When defense investors are this eager, it's usually a sign that they foresee a market where security is not just a luxury but a necessity.

stories.head: $1.4B added to FY27 space resilience budget
stories.body: The recent markup for the FY27 budget has allocated an additional $1.4 billion to enhance space resilience, reflecting a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space capabilities. This increase will likely fund various initiatives, including satellite protection and infrastructure upgrades, as the U.S. seeks to fortify its position in an increasingly contested domain.
stories.soWhat: This budget boost indicates that lawmakers are finally connecting the dots between space and national security, which could lead to more robust funding cycles in the future.

watchlist.title: Watch for more acquisitions in space
watchlist.body: As companies like Rocket Lab demonstrate, acquisitions could become a key strategy for growth amidst rising competition.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
